# fp tracker snapshot

**Generated by `data-raw/snapshot-tracker.sh` on 2026-09-05.**
75 issues. Do not hand-edit: the next run overwrites this file
wholesale, exactly as `data-raw/generate_unicode_tables.R` overwrites the
committed `src/unicode_tables_*.cpp`.

`.fp/` is gitignored, so this file is the only copy of the tracker in
git. It is a backstop for the PUNY-* citations in
`DECISIONS.md`, `AGENTS.md` and the test suite, not a replacement for the tracker: `fp` remains
authoritative and `fp context <id>` remains the way to read an issue.

## PUNY-aaheyvva: Refresh stale release-version references in _pkgdown.yml and .zenodo.json

**Status:** done

### Description

Two small stale-version references noticed during PUNY-zatcuoix (G) and kept out of it as unrelated to the version-as-parameter model:

- `_pkgdown.yml:70-71` pins the news release link to punycoder 1.2.0.
- `.zenodo.json` carries `"version": "1.2.0"`.

Both are release paperwork rather than documentation of behavior, so the natural time to fix them is the 1.3.0 release prep, alongside the DESCRIPTION version bump off 1.2.1.9000. Worth checking at that point whether either is regenerated automatically -- note `.github/workflows/codemeta.yaml` regenerates codemeta.json on push to main via codemetar, so confirm whether .zenodo.json has a comparable generator before hand-editing it.

### Comments

#### 2026-07-26 — 142225707+bart-turczynski@users.noreply.github.com

PR #94 open. Both references now name 1.2.1.

Chose 1.2.1, not 1.3.0: DESCRIPTION is 1.2.1.9000, latest tag is v1.2.1, and CRAN has 1.2.1 -- during development these files should name the last ACTUAL release, and 1.3.0 does not exist yet.

Generator question, checked rather than assumed as the issue asked: neither file has one. .github/workflows/codemeta.yaml regenerates codemeta.json via codemetar (which is why codemeta.json is already current at 1.2.1.9000), but there is no equivalent for .zenodo.json or _pkgdown.yml.

Kept .zenodo.json's version field explicit rather than deleting it. Zenodo's GitHub integration DOES fall back to the release tag when the field is absent, which would make it self-maintaining -- but it records the tag verbatim, i.e. 'v1.2.1' rather than '1.2.1', and this is citation metadata on a published DOI (10.5281/zenodo.20973629). Not worth a v-prefixed version string in the archive record.

Since nothing keeps them current, added a release-time guard to the existing news-version workflow instead of leaving the next drift to be caught by accident. It skips .9000 development versions and only fires on a release version, so it will fail loudly during 1.3.0 prep until both files move -- which is exactly the moment this issue identified as the right one. Verified in both directions against the current tree (passes at 1.2.1, fails for both files at a simulated 1.3.0); YAML/JSON syntax validated.

#### 2026-07-26 — 142225707+bart-turczynski@users.noreply.github.com

Merged to main as 78e1599 (PR #94). Full CI green.

Carry-forward for 1.3.0 release prep: the new guard in .github/workflows/news-version.yaml will FAIL once DESCRIPTION drops its .9000 suffix, until both .zenodo.json and the _pkgdown.yml news.releases entry are moved to 1.3.0. That is intentional -- it turns this issue's silent drift into a blocking check at exactly the right moment.




## PUNY-ahtemhwv: Move punycoder's public identity from GitHub to GitLab

**Status:** done

### Description

The GitHub account hosting punycoder is suspended, so every URL naming it 404s -- including `DESCRIPTION`'s `URL:` and `BugReports:`, which CRAN reads and checks. punycoder is #2 in the seven-package submission order, so this is a release blocker.

Its GitLab project is already `visibility: public` with `issues_access_level: enabled`, so this is the same change rurl made in `0df6cce` (RURL-sgkplmot).

### Done

Repointed `DESCRIPTION`, `CITATION.cff`, `codemeta.json`, `_pkgdown.yml`, `README.Rmd`/`README.md`, `vignettes/punycoder-intro.Rmd`, `.zenodo.json` and the regenerated `man/punycoder-package.Rd`. In-repo document links became repository-relative.

Three URLs were dropped rather than replaced, no live equivalent existing: the pkgdown site (no publisher; GitLab Pages here is `private` and has never deployed), the GitHub Actions / Codecov badges, and the r-universe entry.

Gate: `lintr::lint_package()` clean, `R CMD check --as-cran` 0 errors / 0 warnings / 1 NOTE. The NOTE flags `/-/issues` as 404, which is GitLab-wide anti-scraping against logged-out clients and is the same expected NOTE rurl carries -- it must not be 'fixed'.

- `dev/tracker-snapshot.md` and `dev/user_story.md` (10 refs) -- internal notes.
- r-universe still serves a build of 1.2.1.9000 sourced from the suspended GitHub repo, so it can never update. Restoring it means re-registering the universe against GitLab.

### Comments

#### 2026-08-12 — bartek@turczynski.pl

Merged as ec2643c (MR !1). R CMD check --as-cran: 0 errors, 0 warnings, 1 NOTE (the GitLab-wide /-/issues 404 for logged-out clients, plus the dev-version string) -- both expected. Left open elsewhere: .bestpractices.json (46 refs, needs a BadgeApp re-upload), dev/ notes, and re-registering r-universe against GitLab.

## PUNY-cewysjxi: Decide the predicate contract for ill-formed UTF-8 (is_punycode / is_idn vs the rest of the surface)

**Status:** done

### Description

Split out of the PUNY-ktbbdbho cleanup batch rather than resolved inside it: this is a contract question about exported behavior, not a tidy-up.

### What prompted it

The batch proposed adding perl = TRUE to is_punycode() for consistency with is_idn(). Rejected -- is_punycode() is a lexical xn-- marker predicate, PCRE adds no matching capability it needs, and the change would flip exported behavior on malformed input. But chasing that down surfaced a real inconsistency underneath.

### Observed behavior (R 4.6.1, UTF-8 locale, punycoder at c076d20)

Input                          is_punycode   is_idn          host_normalize / validate_domain / puny_*
latin1-MARKED 'cafe.com'       FALSE  (ok)   TRUE  (ok)      encodes correctly (ok)
unmarked native bytes          FALSE         warns, FALSE    NA
UTF-8-MARKED but ill-formed    TRUE silently warns, FALSE    NA

Ill-formed case is 'xn--a' + ED A0 80 (an encoded UTF-16 surrogate).

Three different answers to the same malformed input across one package's surface: silently accept, warn and reject, reject as NA.

### Two things that are NOT the problem

1. Marked non-UTF-8 encodings. The predicates already handle these correctly -- R's regex engine transcodes a marked latin1 string before matching, so is_idn() sees the non-ASCII byte and is_punycode() does not false-positive. No enc2utf8() call is needed for this case, contrary to how the gap was first described.

2. enc2utf8() as the fix. It is provably a no-op for ill-formed UTF-8: identical(enc2utf8(bad), bad) is TRUE and validUTF8(bad) stays FALSE. It transcodes strings MARKED as latin1/native; it does not repair or reject bytes already marked UTF-8. So 'just call enc2utf8() in the predicates like everything else does' would change nothing here.

The gap is specifically about ill-formed UTF-8, and about unmarked native bytes in a UTF-8 locale (where enc2utf8() is also a no-op because native is assumed to already be UTF-8).

### The decision

What should a predicate return for input that is not valid UTF-8?

a) Document current behavior and leave it. The predicates are lexical and best-effort by design; validation belongs to validate_domain(). Cheapest, but leaves is_punycode() silently reporting TRUE for a string the rest of the package refuses to process.
b) Return NA for invalid UTF-8, matching host_normalize()'s existing 'invalid data is NA, never an abort' contract. Consistent, but the predicates currently return a strictly logical vector, so callers doing if (is_punycode(x)) would start hitting 'missing value where TRUE/FALSE needed'.
c) Make it strict-aware. Neither predicate takes a strict argument today, so this widens the API for a narrow case.

Whichever way it goes, is_punycode() and is_idn() should agree with each other, and the answer should be stated in the roxygen -- the current is_punycode() comment explains why perl is absent but does not say what the function promises for malformed input.

### Notes

- AGENTS.md documents the strict/non-strict split and host_normalize()'s separate NA contract, but says nothing about the predicates. Whatever is decided belongs there too.
- Add coverage under test-contracts.R (NA/error policy) rather than test-validators.R.
- Reproduction script used for the table above is worth recreating as a test fixture; build the byte sequences with rawToChar(as.raw(...)) since source-level escapes get mangled by the shell.

### Comments

#### 2026-07-25 — 142225707+bart-turczynski@users.noreply.github.com

Resolved as option (d) — both predicates return FALSE for ill-formed UTF-8. Landed in #79 (f6aa479).

### Decision rationale

Not one of the issue's original three options. (b) NA was the closest contender and was rejected on evidence, not taste. Surveyed what comparable tools actually do:

**In R** — no string predicate returns NA for ill-formed UTF-8. `validUTF8()` and `validEnc()` answer FALSE; `grepl()`/`startsWith()`/`stringi::stri_detect_*`/`stringr::str_detect` all return logicals; `nchar()`, `toupper()`, `stri_length()` error instead. NA appears only opt-in (`nchar(allowNA = TRUE)`). The split is consistent: detection is total, measurement errors.

**Other languages** — JS `URL.canParse()` returns false and never throws (structurally the same predicate); Go `x/net/idna` exposes no boolean predicate at all, only `(string, error)`; ICU reports via a separate `UIDNAInfo.errors` bitmask alongside `UErrorCode`; Rust makes ill-formed input unrepresentable via `&str`, mapping stray bytes to U+FFFD; Python/Java/.NET fail at the decode boundary before IDNA runs.

No IDNA library in any surveyed language returns a third truth value from a boolean predicate. The option exists here only because R has NA. Meanwhile `host_normalize()` returning NA is well-precedented precisely because it returns a *value*, where NA is a natural "absent" — a distinction that does not transfer to a predicate.

### Correction to the issue's framing

The issue describes "three different answers to the same malformed input across one package's surface" as if it were a design inconsistency. It was not a design decision at all: `is_punycode()` matched with R's default TRE engine (bytewise, hence TRUE) and `is_idn()` used `perl = TRUE`, where PCRE validates UTF-8 first (hence warn + FALSE). Two of the three answers were inherited verbatim from base R's two regex engines.

Also confirmed: `is_punycode` warns on unmarked native bytes, which the issue's table recorded as silent.

### Implementation note worth keeping

The gate is `enc2utf8()` **then** `validUTF8()`, shared by both predicates via `.detect_valid_utf8()` in `R/helpers.R`. Both halves are load-bearing:

- `enc2utf8()` alone is a no-op on bytes already marked UTF-8 — exactly as the issue said, so it detects nothing.
- `validUTF8()` alone inspects raw bytes, so it regresses `is_idn()` on a string merely *marked* latin1 from TRUE to FALSE — one of the two cases the issue explicitly listed as NOT the problem.

The first implementation used `validUTF8()` alone and broke the latin1 case; the new tests caught it on the first run. Both are now covered in `test-contracts.R`.

Side effect, not a suppression: the spurious `is_idn()` warning is gone because ill-formed bytes never reach PCRE.

### Scope confirmations

- Revdeps: CRAN lists `pslr` and `rurl` as reverse imports. Neither calls either predicate anywhere in code (only prose in `ACKNOWLEDGMENTS.md`). No coupled release ordering needed, unlike the 1.2.0 `strict` change.
- Filed under **Breaking changes** in NEWS.md — exported behavior changed, malformed input or not.
- Contract recorded in AGENTS.md as a third contract alongside strict/non-strict and `host_normalize`'s NA policy.
- `"bytes"`-marked strings now answer FALSE instead of TRUE, without erroring, so the "never throws" promise holds.

### Verification

468 tests passing, 0 failures, 1 environmental skip; lintr clean; `R CMD check --as-cran` 1 NOTE (standing dev-version note only); all 11 CI checks green.

### Release timing

Lands on main now but ships in 1.3.0. punycoder 1.2.1 published to CRAN 2026-07-19, and CRAN policy is "no more than every 1–2 months", so the next submission window opens ~2026-08-19 regardless. The dev NEWS already carries a Breaking changes section (URL surface removal, PUNY-rumdaymk), making that release the natural carrier — users must read its NEWS anyway, and bundling avoids a second release where a predicate flips under them.




## PUNY-cqnvjakw: Add @examples to punycoder-package.Rd + align @keywords internal with fleet

**Status:** done

### Description

`val.meter` (pharmaR) scores `help_examples_coverage` as
`help_pages_with_examples_count / length(Rd_db)` with **no filtering** — the
auto-generated `<pkg>-package.Rd` stub counts in the denominator. It is the only
punycoder page without `\examples{}` (8 of 9 pages have them), so it alone holds
the metric at 0.889.

**Verified avoidable.** Adding `@examples` to the `_PACKAGE` roxygen block in
`R/punycoder-package.R` and re-running `roxygen2::roxygenise()` emits a real
`\examples{}` section; tested on a sandbox copy of rurl, where the metric then
reported 1.0.

#### Second, separate finding
`punycoder-package.Rd` has **no `\keyword{internal}`**, unlike rurl, pslr,
pagerankr and seor, whose package stubs all carry it. That is a divergence from
the rest of the fleet — worth aligning while touching this file.

#### Caveat
The example runs under `R CMD check`, so it must be valid and fast.




## PUNY-cwtxlabr: Single-pass looks_like_url_input (gated on the profiling run)

**Status:** done

### Description

Split out of the PUNY-ktbbdbho cleanup batch so closing that batch does not drop it. Same treatment PUNY-zgaqusnu already got.

looks_like_url_input (src/punycoder_domain.cpp:147-179) scans the string up to six times -- separate find calls for '://', '/', '?', '#', '@', ':'. One pass would do. It runs per element on every puny_encode/puny_decode call, so it is on the hot path.

**Do not land this speculatively.** It is explicitly gated on the profiling run that also gates PUNY-fsaaigwl. Two reasons to expect it may come back a no-op:

- The profile that motivated the batch predates PUNY-thyalpud (skip redundant per-label NFC), which already removed most of the cost it pointed at.
- Six find() calls over a short host string is a handful of cache-resident byte scans; it is plausible this never shows up at all.

If the profile does not show it, close as won't-do and record the measurement. Measure against a clean -O2 build per AGENTS.md -- never under devtools::test(), which compiles at -O0.

### Comments

#### 2026-07-24 — 142225707+bart-turczynski@users.noreply.github.com

Merged as 14c8dc0 (PR #77) -- but NOT as specified. The measurement inverted the issue's premise.

The proposed single-pass rewrite is a PESSIMIZATION: 0.81x, i.e. slower than the six scans it replaces. Each find() lowers to a vectorized memchr; a byte-at-a-time scalar loop cannot compete on host-length strings no matter how many passes it saves.

What does help is deletion. find("://") and rfind("//", 0) are provably redundant -- both forms contain a '/', which the marker scan below already rejects. Removing them keeps every remaining scan vectorized.

Bake-off, best-of-15 over 800k calls, bare-host corpus (the FALSE arm):
  current (6 scans)          14.30 ms  1.00x
  single-pass scalar (as proposed) 17.58 ms  0.81x
  find_first_of("/?#@")       9.75 ms  1.47x
  table-driven single pass    9.21 ms  1.55x
  drop redundant scans (landed) 9.22 ms  1.55x

The table-driven pass ties but costs far more code, so the deletion wins on speed and simplicity both.

Independent confirmation: profiling puny_encode over a 20k-host corpus, the guard's subtree share falls 7.21% -> 4.78% of process time. That ratio (610/399 = 1.53x) reproduces the microbenchmark's 1.55x from a different measurement path.

Equivalence: 0 mismatches vs the current implementation across an exhaustive sweep of all strings up to length 4 over an 11-char alphabet covering every branch (16,105 inputs) plus 2,000,000 randomized inputs up to 60 bytes over the full byte range.

So: the issue's fallback prediction ("may come back a no-op, close as won't-do") was also wrong -- the guard was genuinely 7.2% of the path. It was the proposed fix that was wrong, not the target.

Verified on a clean -O2 build per AGENTS.md, never under devtools::test(). 450 tests, R CMD check --as-cran 1 NOTE (dev-version only), CI green.




## PUNY-czleeqwz: Multi-version Unicode support: make the pinned table set a selectable dimension

**Status:** done

### Description

Turn the Unicode version from a **hardcoded pin** into a **first-class, selectable
dimension** so more than one Unicode version can be built into the package and
chosen by the caller.

Today the version is baked into filenames, a C++ namespace, a header guard, and
16 call sites. Bumping it is a rename-and-sweep across ~19 files; having *two*
versions available at once is not expressible at all. That is the gap this epic
closes.

### Why now: the Unicode 17.0 dry run

Unicode 17.0 shipped 2025-09-09 (4,803 new characters, 159,801 total; 4 new
scripts; CJK Extension J with 4,298 ideographs). A full 17.0.0 dry run was done
in a scratch tree (repo untouched) and the result is strong:

- **The generator ran with zero assertions firing.** Every derived-invariant
  guard held: the all-1,114,112-code-point trie verification, the composition
  sorted-partition check, the ASCII-bound shape assertions on the mark/joining
  tables, the `nfc_inert` bound, and the NFC_QC-vs-composition-pair cross-check.
- **The generator is reproducible.** Re-running at 16.0.0 reproduced the
  committed `src/unicode_tables_16_0_0.cpp` byte-for-byte.
- **Fully conformant against the 17.0.0 corpus**: 59 deviations, every one the
  already-documented A4_2 trailing-root-dot divergence. Zero false rejections.
- **Suite result: 4 failures**, all bookkeeping — the `"16.0.0"` version pin in
  `test-normalize.R:221`, and 3 rows in `test-idna-conformance.R` that come from
  running a Unicode 17 engine against the 16.0.0-vintage `IdnaTestV2.txt`
  fixture. All 3 trace to a single character, `U+32931` (CJK Ext J), which is
  `disallowed` in 16.0 and `valid` in 17.0 — it appears once as a U-label and
  twice as its A-label `xn--20-9802c`.
- **The tables got smaller and no slower.** The auto-derived UTS-46 mapping trie
  re-chose its own shape: block 64 -> 128, stage1 `14344 x uint16_t` ->
  `7172 x uint8_t`, 77.9 KB -> 70.8 KB. The `.so` shrank 463,776 -> 447,264
  bytes. `host_normalize` throughput is flat across ascii/unicode/mixed at
  n=100,000. This is ADR-011/ADR-012 paying off exactly as designed.

### The bump is provably accept-only

A code-point-level diff of `IdnaMappingTable.txt` 16.0.0 -> 17.0.0:

```
disallowed -> valid        4774
disallowed -> mapped         29   (e.g. U+A7CE, U+A7D2, U+A7D4)
                     total  4803
```

4,803 is exactly the number of characters Unicode 17 added, and **every
transition starts from `disallowed`**. Nothing valid/mapped/ignored/deviation
moved. This matches the UTS #46 stability guarantee verbatim: mapping tables
"will always be backward compatible with previous versions of the table: only
characters with the Status value **disallowed** may change in Status or Mapping
value."

So a version bump can only ever **newly accept** a host, never start rejecting
one that used to normalize. That is what makes multi-version support tractable:
the versions are ordered by permissiveness, not mutually contradictory.

### Standards position

UTS #46 sets no "best version". All three conformance clauses are phrased
*"Given a version of Unicode..."* — the version is a **parameter of
conformance**, not fixed by the spec. The current pinned-version design is the
conformant approach, and making the pin selectable stays conformant. UTS #46
revision 35 was reissued for Unicode 17.0.

### Scope

In scope: generator parameterization, per-version table units that can coexist,
a runtime selection mechanism, profile-identity threading, per-version
conformance fixtures, and a shipped-versions policy.

Out of scope: **UTS #39**. Unicode 17 reclassified 77,838 Han characters from
allowed to restricted and Bopomofo to limited-use, but that is
`Identifier_Status` / security-profile territory. punycoder implements UTS #46
and does not consult those tables (see PUNY-mjdrwxne, confusables as explicit
non-goal). Noted here only so it is not mistaken for a UTS-46 change.

### Open questions

1. **How many versions ship?** Each table set is ~70-100 KB of `.rodata`. Two is
   cheap; N is a CRAN tarball and compile-time cost. Likely answer: current +
   previous, not an archive.
2. **Selection mechanism.** A `host_normalize(unicode_version =)` argument, a
   `getOption("punycoder.unicode_version")`, or both? Note `host_normalize` is
   deliberately *not* on the strict/non-strict switch, so a new global option
   needs its own justification.
3. **Does the profile token change?** `uts46-nontransitional-std3-v1` is read by
   `pslr` as a reproducibility key, and `normalization_profile_info()` already
   reports `unicode_version` as a separate column (PUNY-nblrvplp). Leaning: the
   *profile* is unchanged (still non-transitional, STD3, same flags), so keep
   `v1` and let the version column carry the difference. Must be confirmed with
   `pslr` before it ships.
4. **Default version.** Newest available, or the conservative pin? Since bumps
   are accept-only, newest is the safe default — but it does change results for
   downstreams.

### Sequencing

The CRAN release trio (pslr 1.1.1 -> punycoder 1.2.1 -> rurl 2.7.0) is
serialized on CRAN publication and punycoder is at 1.2.1.9000. This work changes
accepted-input behaviour for downstreams — land it **after** the trio clears
(see PUNY-eprrzmxt), not into it.


### Comments

#### 2026-07-26 — 142225707+bart-turczynski@users.noreply.github.com

Epic complete — all seven children done (A PUNY-womoymke, B PUNY-kfpxsquq, C PUNY-wjlfpppq, D PUNY-qfautzhz, E PUNY-lirlisix, F PUNY-odzyvuru, G PUNY-zatcuoix), shipped across PRs #84-#92.

Answers to the four open questions, as they actually landed:
1. How many ship? CURRENT + PREVIOUS (16.0.0 and 17.0.0), with a one-release deprecation cycle before a set is dropped. Not an archive: two sets cost ~1 MB of .so plus +776 KB of vendored corpus, ~2.4 MB installed, no R CMD check size NOTE. (ADR-017)
2. Selection mechanism? host_normalize(unicode_version =) ONLY. Deliberately no getOption() form: punycoder.strict is error POLICY, the Unicode version is profile IDENTITY, and ambient identity breaks reproducibility keys. NULL means the pin — never 'newest', which would change behavior under a caller when a set is added. An unshipped version errors with the available list rather than falling back. (ADR-016)
3. Does the profile token change? YES, v1 -> v2 — but because the PIN MOVED, not because a version became selectable. The bare token means 'whatever the pin is', so without the bump one string would denote two Unicode versions across the release. Selecting a non-default version does not bump -vN; it appends, e.g. uts46-nontransitional-std3-v2+unicode-16.0.0. (ADR-017)
4. Default version? NEWEST SHIPPED (17.0.0). Verified accept-only by measurement, not by the stability guarantee alone: over both vendored corpora x 8 flag combinations the new default matches explicit 17.0.0 in all 102,448 comparisons and differs from 16.0.0 on 3 rows (16.0.0 corpus) and 5 rows (17.0.0 corpus), every one NA -> value, zero changed values.

The dry run's predictions held on the real bump: generator reproducible at 16.0.0 byte-for-byte, zero assertions fired, the UTS-46 mapping trie re-chose its own shape (block 64 -> 128) with no hand edit, and conformance came out at the documented A4_2 root-dot deviation only (57 at 16.0.0, 59 at 17.0.0, pinned per version).

Not in this epic and still open downstream: PSLR-fjkaqckg (reship pslr's bundled index, hard-gated on punycoder 1.3.0 reaching CRAN) and RURL-csdmuguh (assert the inherited pin, bump the Remotes dev pin). Neither requires punycoder changes.

## PUNY-dopcsyjw: Port rurl's verify-on-push mirror predicate: the archival push is guarded by an AGENTS.md sentence instead of by the hook

**Status:** todo

### Description

## The pre-push verify gate has no mirror predicate, so the archival push is guarded by a convention instead of by code

Found while pushing PUNY-tacfinef and PUNY-jzxomoqq, 2026-09-05. punycoder's instance of
rurl's RURL-qkowfsdt, which is already fixed there.

### What is here now

`.pre-commit-config.yaml` spells the gate inline, with `always_run: true` and no predicate
on the destination:

    - id: verify
      name: verify (mirrors CI)
      entry: Rscript -e
      args:
        - 'lints <- lintr::lint_package(); ...; rcmdcheck::rcmdcheck(args = "--as-cran", error_on = "warning")'
      always_run: true
      stages: [pre-push]

So it fires for every destination, `backup` included — the local bare mirror at
`~/Projects/_backups/punycoder.git`, which only ever receives history that already passed
on its way to `origin`. The gate there verifies nothing.

Nothing in the repo prevents that. What prevents it is a sentence in AGENTS.md:

> Push to `backup` with `--no-verify`: a mirror must capture whatever state exists,
> including a red one.

### Why that is the wrong shape

rurl's wrapper header makes the argument better than I can, and it is the reason this is
worth filing rather than leaving as a documented convention:

> a gate that fires where it cannot help is a gate people learn to `--no-verify` past
> — including where it can.

The instruction teaches the habit. `--no-verify` is not scoped to the mirror by anything
except the reader remembering which push they are doing, and the gate costs minutes
(measured twice today: full `lintr` + `R CMD check --as-cran` per push), so the incentive
runs the wrong way.

### What does NOT apply here — checked, not assumed

rurl's third argument was that a gate run **mutates the working tree** (it rewrites
`tests/testthat/_snaps/` and can touch byte-pinned fixtures), so an archival push could
dirty the tree. **That does not hold for punycoder.** There is no `tests/testthat/_snaps/`
in this package, and `git status` was clean after both gate runs today. The case here rests
on wasted minutes and the `--no-verify` habit alone, which is weaker — hence low priority.

### The fix, already written next door

`rurl/tools/verify-on-push.sh` (RURL-qkowfsdt): a committed wrapper that pre-commit calls
as `entry:`, which reads the destination pre-commit re-exports as `$PRE_COMMIT_REMOTE_URL`
and skips only when the destination is a directory on this filesystem:

    -d "$url"  ->  a path on this machine  ->  a mirror  ->  skip
    otherwise  ->  a transport (ssh/https/git)  ->  a forge  ->  run the gate

Keyed on the URL, deliberately not on the remote *name*: a name is a local alias, so
keying on the string `backup` would leave the skip silently attached to the wrong remote
after a `git remote rename`. Anything the predicate cannot positively identify as a local
mirror runs the gate — it is a scoped skip, not a hole.

Porting it also moves the gate definition out of a YAML string into a reviewable file that
can be run by hand and listed with `--list`, which is the other half of what rurl gained.

### Done when

- [ ] Pushing to `backup` does not run the gate, without `--no-verify`
- [ ] Pushing to `origin` runs it unchanged, and so does any destination the predicate
      cannot identify as a local mirror
- [ ] The AGENTS.md sentence instructing `--no-verify` is removed, since the reason for it is gone

## PUNY-dvddthjy: Add A-label round-trip validation on strict decode (RFC 5891 canonical form)

**Status:** done

### Description

RFC 5891 / UTS-46 require that a decoded A-label re-encodes to exactly the same A-label (canonical form: no uppercase in the payload, valid Punycode, etc.). punycode_decode_label_fallback (src/punycoder_algorithm.cpp:193) and the libidn2 decode path do not verify this round-trip.

has_uppercase_payload (src/punycoder_backend.cpp:95-100) routes uppercase payloads to the fallback, but there is no canonical round-trip check anywhere, so non-canonical xn-- inputs decode silently in strict mode. This is the one real spec-compliance gap in the decoder; the encode/decode math itself is correct.

Proposed fix (strict mode only):
- After decoding label L to Unicode U, re-encode U and require it to equal the original A-label (case-insensitive on the xn-- prefix, exact on payload). If it differs, throw invalid_punycode_label.
- Keep non-strict mode lenient (best-effort decode) to preserve current behavior for tolerant callers.

This is a strictness/correctness enhancement, not a hot-path change. Coordinate with the non-strict length-bound issue so both share the validation entry point if convenient.

Acceptance: strict decode rejects non-canonical A-labels (e.g. ones whose round-trip differs); valid canonical labels are unaffected; non-strict behavior unchanged.

### Comments

#### 2026-06-05 — 142225707+bart-turczynski@users.noreply.github.com

Fixed in 9a36591 (branch fix/decode-label-bounds-canonical). Strict decode now re-encodes the decoded label and requires a byte-exact payload match (xn-- prefix compared case-insensitively) via plan_label_transform; throws invalid_punycode_label on mismatch. Non-strict stays lenient. Updated the case-insensitive test in test-encoding.R (uppercase payloads now rejected in strict per the issue) and added canonical round-trip tests. All 278 tests pass.




## PUNY-dzvonwoh: Replicate rurl's OpenSSF Best Practices passing badge to siblings (max out everything)

**Status:** done

### Description

Replicate rurl's OpenSSF Best Practices **passing** badge setup to the sibling packages so they also reach 100%. rurl earned the badge (bestpractices.dev project 13394) via an in-repo `.bestpractices.json`. Two child issues track each package: **punycoder** and **pslr**.

### Source of truth / template
- rurl's `.bestpractices.json` (repo root, `.Rbuildignore`d) is the template. Copy it and change per-repo facts: package name, **every URL** (repo, pkgdown, CRAN, CONTRIBUTING / LICENSE / SECURITY / NEWS / issues / security-advisories, CI workflow paths), version, maintainer email.
- rurl's `SECURITY.md` is the template for the security policy.

### The "max out everything" rule (the key finding)
The badge is awarded at **100%**. To hit 100% you must give **every** criterion a definitive answer (Met / Unmet / N/A) — **including SUGGESTED criteria**. Leaving even one SUGGESTED criterion at `?` (unknown) parks the score at 99%. (On rurl the last 1% was `dynamic_analysis_enable_assertions` sitting at `?`.)

### Criteria gotchas learned on rurl
1. **"(URL required)" criteria** will NOT validate as Met from prose alone — every justification must contain an `https://` URL. rurl's file already does this throughout; keep it when copying.
2. **`dynamic_analysis_enable_assertions` rejects `N/A`** ("not included in the list"). Valid answers are Met / Unmet / `?` only. Set **Met** (testthat expectations are runtime assertions during dynamic analysis; rhub ASAN/UBSAN/valgrind adds memory/UB assertions). Never N/A.
3. **N/A for these libs:** `crypto_*` (no crypto), `hardening` + `sites_password_security` (not a web app). BUT see the next point.
4. **COMPILED CODE CHANGES THINGS.** Unlike rurl (pure R), **both punycoder and pslr ship C/C++ in `src/`**. So `dynamic_analysis_unsafe` is **NOT N/A** for them — they contain memory-unsafe code and the criterion requires routine dynamic memory-safety tooling. Both already have an rhub workflow; wire it with `clang-asan` + `valgrind` and mark `dynamic_analysis_unsafe` **Met** (cite those runs), not N/A.

### Supporting repo changes (per package)
- Add `.bestpractices.json` at repo root + an `.Rbuildignore` entry (`^\.bestpractices\.json$`).
- Add/verify `SECURITY.md` + `.Rbuildignore` entry, and **enable free GitHub private vulnerability reporting**: `gh api --method PUT repos/OWNER/REPO/private-vulnerability-reporting` — free on public repos, **zero Actions usage** (does not touch the deployment-check quota). Makes the `vulnerability_report_*` criteria Met.
- Wire dynamic analysis into the existing `rhub.yaml`: add `clang-asan,valgrind` to the workflow config default. It's manual `workflow_dispatch`, so **no recurring Actions minutes**. For these compiled packages this is genuinely meaningful.
- Register the project at bestpractices.dev to obtain a project ID, then add the badge to `README.Rmd` and re-render `README.md` via `devtools::build_readme()` (the README-sync CI check will fail otherwise).

### BadgeApp ingest workflow
- Edit mode → **"Save (and continue) 🤖"** re-ingests `.bestpractices.json`.
- Proposals are **unforced**: they only fill blank/`?` fields and never overwrite an existing value (conflicts show a blue ≠ marker). To make the file win on a populated field, reset that field to `?` first or edit it by hand, then Save.
- Review highlighted changes, Save, repeat until 100%.

### Out of scope here
- Silver/Gold (rurl tracks that in RURL-nuudihaq) and the OSPS **Baseline Series** (a separate track that ties to `SECURITY-INSIGHTS.yml`, rurl RURL-uakixclb).

### Reference
rurl PRs: #64 (initial), #65 (URLs + enable_assertions), #66, #67 (README badge), #68 (enable_assertions → Met).




## PUNY-egaqhtnc: puny_encode/puny_decode/validate_domain mishandle non-UTF-8 (latin1) input

**Status:** done

### Description

`host_normalize()` calls `enc2utf8(x)` (R/normalize.R:62); no other entry point does. `Rcpp::as<std::string>` then hands raw latin1 bytes to the C++ UTF-8 decoder, so the same string gets four different answers:

```
## x <- "café.com" with Encoding(x) <- "latin1"
host_normalize   xn--caf-dma.com
puny_encode      ERROR: Error encoding domain: Truncated UTF-8 sequence
validate_domain  FALSE
is_idn           TRUE
```

Hits anyone in a non-UTF-8 locale, or reading latin1-marked strings out of read.csv().

### Fix
`enc2utf8()` at the R boundary: `.call_with_validation()` (R/helpers.R:40) and `validate_domain()` (R/validators.R:81). Also `.compare_backends()` for parity.

### Safety check (done)
`enc2utf8()` is a byte-exact no-op on input already marked UTF-8, verified against deliberately-malformed bytes. So `helper-validation.R::raw_utf8()` fixtures still reach the native UTF-8 validator and the existing ill-formed-UTF-8 tests keep their meaning.

### Tests
All three functions, strict and non-strict, mixed vectors, plus a regression asserting the existing malformed-bytes inputs still error/NA as before.

### Comments

#### 2026-07-24 — 142225707+bart-turczynski@users.noreply.github.com

Starting implementation on a focused fix branch. First pass: normalize character inputs to UTF-8 at the R-to-C++ boundary and add Latin-1 regression coverage while preserving malformed-byte validation.

#### 2026-07-24 — 142225707+bart-turczynski@users.noreply.github.com

Implemented UTF-8 transcoding in .call_with_validation(), validate_domain(), and .compare_backends(). Added Latin-1 coverage for strict/non-strict calls, mixed encodings, backend parity, and malformed-byte preservation. Clean -O2 installed-package suite passes: 394 passed, 2 expected offline skips.

#### 2026-07-24 — 142225707+bart-turczynski@users.noreply.github.com

Additional boundary bug confirmed from the new regression: native Unicode output carried UTF-8 bytes but Rcpp proxy assignment marked it as unknown, unsafe on non-UTF-8 locales. Fixed transform_strings() and backend comparison outputs with explicit CE_UTF8 markers. Fresh -O2 full suite: 400 passed, 2 expected offline skips.

## PUNY-emjvtzlr: Standards-compliance audit: scope decided (resolvability/safety-agnostic IDNA primitive)

**Status:** done

### Description

## Standards-compliance audit: scope decided

Audit of punycoder against the IDN / Punycode / URL standards landscape, turned
into a set of **scope and documentation decisions**.

### Deciding principle (settled)

> **punycoder is the standards primitive for domain-label and host-name
> normalization: RFC 3492 Punycode plus a pinned UTS #46 non-transitional IDNA
> profile. It is agnostic about DNS existence, PSL/registrability, URL
> canonicalization, browser-compatibility policy, registry policy, and
> spoof/display safety. Those opinions belong upstack.**

Operational definition of what the package does:

> Given a Unicode domain/host-name string, produce a deterministic,
> standards-profiled **ASCII comparison form**, or reject / return `NA` if the
> input is invalid under that profile.

**Terminology:** "canonicalization" is overloaded — avoid it for punycoder.
This package does **host normalization** (IDNA/UTS-46); **URL canonicalization**
is `rurl`'s word. "Standards-pure" means resolvability- and safety-agnostic, not
domain-agnostic: Punycode *is* a domain technology.

#### What punycoder owns
UTS #46 mapping, NFC, A-label/U-label validation, Punycode (Bootstring)
conversion, DNS label/host length checks, root-dot behaviour, pinned Unicode
data, backend-independent output (libidn2 must not change accept/reject or
output), and a named reproducibility profile.

#### What punycoder does NOT own
URL canonicalization, a named WHATWG/browser host-policy "mode", percent
encode/decode, default-port/path behaviour, DNS resolvability, PSL/registrability
classification (→ `pslr`), registry restrictions, spoof/homograph safety,
display policy, or any "is this safe/real/canonical on the web?" judgment.

#### Layering and the circular-dependency corollary
Strictly one-directional: `rurl` (URL canonicalization / browser policy) and
`pslr` (PSL/registrability classification) sit **upstack** and consume
`host_normalize()`; opinions never flow down. (`pslr` is PSL/registrability, not
"resolvability" — it does not perform DNS resolution.)

The earlier `rurl` ↔ `punycoder` circular dependency was a **scope symptom**, not
a build problem. CRAN forbids cyclic *strong* deps (`Depends`/`Imports`/
`LinkingTo`): a cycle has no valid build order, so the package is uninstallable
from clean and CRAN rejects it. (Cyclic `Suggests` are legal — the only shape a
back-reference could take, conditional/test-only.) punycoder wanted something
*from* rurl only because the URL surface (item C) was reaching up into rurl's
layer. Move that up and the cycle disappears by construction.

---

### Verdict on the named standards

- **RFC 3492 (Punycode): compliant.** `src/punycoder_algorithm.cpp` is a
  faithful, overflow-guarded port, validated against the §7.1 vectors
  (`inst/testdata/rfc3492_vectors.csv`) under both backends. RFC 3492 defines
  **Bootstring** (a general parameterized algorithm); "Punycode" is the IDNA
  parameterization, and the `xn--` A-label framing / A-label–U-label vocabulary
  come from RFC 5890/5891, not 3492.
- **`host_normalize()` — NOT "RFC 5891 / IDNA2008 compliant".** It implements a
  **pinned UTS #46 non-transitional ToASCII profile with IDNA2008-derived
  checks**. UTS #46 is *compatibility processing*, deliberately not identical to
  IDNA2008: WHATWG uses UTS #46 "and not IDNA2008", and UTS #46 accepts labels
  IDNA2008 would reject (e.g. `☕.example` → `xn--53h.example`). Describe it as a
  UTS #46 profile, never as IDNA2008 conformance.
- The `puny_*` / `url_*` family is a low-level ACE/Punycode helper + LDH only —
  no UTS #46.

---

### Decision items

#### A. Two-tier split — RESOLVED: document hard, no IDNA routing
`puny_encode`/`puny_decode` are a **low-level ACE/Punycode domain-label helper**:
RFC 3492 Bootstring payload wrapped in the RFC 5890/5891 `xn--` A-label framing,
plus LDH/length/hyphen checks. It is **not** "raw RFC 3492 full stop" and **not
an IDNA normalization API** — no NFC, no UTS #46 mapping, no case-fold of the
Unicode portion, no Bidi/Joiner checks. `host_normalize` is the only IDNA/UTS-46
surface.
- **Decision:** keep the helper non-normalizing (do **not** route `puny_encode`
  through UTS #46 — the raw transform is a legitimate primitive). Tighten
  DESCRIPTION so "RFC 3492 compliant conversion" can't be read as "does IDNA",
  and so the helper reads as "low-level ACE, not IDNA normalization".

#### B. host_normalize is stricter than browsers — RESOLVED: expose narrow UTS #46 flags OR defer; no "browser mode"
`host_normalize` pins `CheckHyphens=true`, `UseSTD3ASCIIRules=true`,
`VerifyDnsLength=true`. WHATWG `domain to ASCII(beStrict=false)` flips **exactly
three** flags: `CheckHyphens=false`, `UseSTD3=false`, `VerifyDnsLength=false`.
**`CheckBidi` and `CheckJoiners` stay `true` even in browser mode** — they are
never part of "relaxed" and must not become knobs. Consequences of our strict
default: we reject `ab--cd.com`, `_dmarc.example.com`, SRV `_sip._tcp.x.com`,
underscore TXT names that real DNS / browsers accept.
- The principle **kills a named "browser mode" in punycoder** — WHATWG/browser
  host policy is `rurl`.
- Two honest options, pick one (don't split the difference and call it "the
  UTS-46 parameter space" — it isn't):
  1. **Narrow:** expose `check_hyphens`, `use_std3`, `verify_dns_length` as
     documented UTS #46 flags, strict defaults, and explicitly state that full
     WHATWG semantics live in `rurl`.
  2. **Defer:** keep the strict profile fixed, document the divergence, and let
     `rurl` own all relaxation.
- **Decision needed:** narrow-flags vs defer. If narrow, the relaxable set is
  precisely those three flags — not Bidi/Joiners.

#### B2. Profile identity must become parametric — NEW, gates B
`normalization_profile_info()` is a **zero-arg report of the default profile**,
returning the opaque token `"uts46-nontransitional-std3-v1"`;
`punycoder_normalize.cpp` notes "v1 always applies the full profile"; `pslr`
reads the token as a reproducibility key. **The moment B exposes any runtime
flag, a zero-arg defaults report can no longer describe the profile a given call
actually used** — one token silently covering two behaviours is a correctness bug
downstack.
- **Decision:** before exposing flags, `normalization_profile_info()` must either
  (a) take matching arguments so it can report the identity for a specific flag
  set, or (b) gain another mechanism to emit the profile identity for the exact
  flags used by a `host_normalize()` call. Either way expose the individual
  parameters (`check_hyphens`, `use_std3`, `verify_dns_length`, `check_bidi`,
  `check_joiners`, `transitional`, `unicode_version`) alongside the token, so
  downstream keys on the parameter set; the token stays a coarse cache key but is
  no longer load-bearing alone. Any parameter or Unicode-data change is a
  behaviour change needing a profile/version story.

#### C. URL parser not RFC 3986 / WHATWG conformant — RESOLVED: best-effort host extraction, move upstack
`punycoder_url.cpp` is a hand-rolled splitter (no percent encode/decode, no
scheme validation, `userinfo` via `find_last_of('@')`, reimplemented IPv4/IPv6;
IPv6 zone-IDs / RFC 6874 unhandled). RFC 3986 / WHATWG have far broader authority
(scheme, host, percent-encoding, port, path, IPv6, serialization) than this
attempts. URL canonicalization is `rurl`'s mission; `host_normalize` survives the
principle, the URL surface does not.
- **Decision:** (a) demote `url_*` / `parse_url` to explicitly-documented
  "best-effort host extraction / rewriting, NOT URL parsing or canonicalization",
  and (b) plan removal in favour of `rurl` consuming punycoder's host functions.
  The one item implying a possible **API reduction**.

#### D. UTS #39 confusables / homograph — RESOLVED: not this package's acceptance criteria
Spoof/homograph and display-safety detection are **not part of punycoder's
acceptance criteria** (not "never relevant"). UTS #46 itself *recommends* UTR #36
/ UTS #39 as additional application/UI checks — which is exactly the argument for
placing them in `rurl` or a dedicated policy layer, not here. Document as an
explicit non-goal so nobody assumes `host_normalize` gives spoof protection.

#### E. No official UTS #46 conformance fixture — DO FIRST
We test RFC 3492 against its official vectors but have **no `IdnaTestV2.txt`**
(Unicode 16.0.0 UCD) — the canonical conformance corpus for the `host_normalize`
pipeline. If the package claims standards-faithful host normalization, passing
this suite is the **receipt for that claim**.
- **Correction (was stale):** the earlier note that `test-normalize.R` shows a
  current contract divergence is wrong. That test asserts the *code* already does
  standard UTS #46 (`xn--MNCHEN-3ya.de` → `xn--mnchen-3ya.de`); the divergence is
  a **defect in `docs/normalization-contract.md §5`**, tracked on PSLR-pwwtqowh —
  not a code bug. IdnaTestV2 remains the right fixture regardless.
- **Flag interaction (for B):** `IdnaTestV2.txt` carries flag-related status
  codes; an implementation with a flag set false **ignores the corresponding
  status codes**. If relaxed flags (B) are exposed, the conformance harness must
  filter status codes per the active flag set.
- **Action:** wire `IdnaTestV2.txt` in. Do this first.

#### F. Uncited / missing canonical docs — DOCUMENT
Three real gaps that name behaviour we already implement:
- **RFC 5892** (*The Unicode Code Points and IDNA*) — derived property values
  (`PVALID`/`DISALLOWED`/`CONTEXTJ`/`CONTEXTO`/`UNASSIGNED`) and contextual rules.
  Cite it because UTS #46 derives part of its validation story from IDNA2008 and
  because our `CheckJoiners` uses the RFC 5892 **ContextJ** rules for ZWJ/ZWNJ
  (`punycoder_normalize.cpp:69-86`, `Joining_Type` tables). **Do NOT claim
  punycoder implements full RFC 5892 CONTEXTO validation — it does not.** Under
  the current UTS #46 profile, IDNA2008 CONTEXTO code points that the mapping
  table marks `valid` (e.g. U+00B7 middle dot `a·b.cat`, Greek keraia U+0375,
  Hebrew geresh/gershayim, Katakana middle dot U+30FB) are accepted with no
  CONTEXTO check. That is **conformant UTS #46** (UTS #46 mandates CheckJoiners,
  not CONTEXTO); adding CONTEXTO would be an intentional, separately-tested
  change, not a bug fix.
- **RFC 5893** (*Right-to-Left Scripts for IDNA*) — **the** Bidi rule (we run
  `CheckBidi` but never cite the source).
- **UAX #15** (*Normalization Forms / NFC*) — NFC is a literal UTS #46 step; we
  cite UAX #44 but not #15.

Already-noted, still document:
- **RFC 5890** (IDNA2008 framework — `xn--` ACE prefix, A/U-label/LDH vocab;
  `puny_encode` emitting `xn--` is RFC 5890, not 3492).
- **RFC 5894** (IDNA2008 rationale, informational) — optional.
- **UAX #44 (UCD)** — `Bidi_Class`, `Joining_Type`, `General_Category`,
  `Canonical_Combining_Class`.
- **STD 3 = RFC 952 + RFC 1123** — source of "UseSTD3ASCIIRules".
- **RFC 8753** — IDNA review for new Unicode versions (rationale for pinning).
- **RFC 3490/3491/3454 (IDNA2003 / Nameprep / Stringprep)** — consciously NOT
  used; UTS #46 non-transitional supersedes. Note as the rejected alternative.
- **Make the UTS #46 ≠ IDNA2008 distinction explicit** next to the RFC 5891
  reference (per the verdict above).

Scope-conditional — belong with the URL surface, so if item C moves it to `rurl`
these citations move too:
- **RFC 3986** (URI), **RFC 3987** (IRI — host-only), **WHATWG URL Standard**,
  **RFC 5952** (IPv6 text form), **RFC 4291** (IPv6 addressing), **RFC 6874**
  (IPv6 zone IDs).

---

### Reference: is Punycode used outside domains?

Functionally **no** — every standardized use is a host-like identifier.
- **Bootstring** is the general algorithm (RFC 3492); "Punycode" is its IDNA
  parameterization. Exposing raw Bootstring would be the theoretical extreme —
  flag as YAGNI, don't build.
- Real-world appearances are all "the domain slot of something": email
  (EAI/SMTPUTF8, RFC 6530/6531/6532 — domain part via A-labels; local part is raw
  UTF-8, *not* punycode), TLS/X.509 names (SNI, `dNSName`), DNS zone data,
  URIs/IRIs. No standardized non-domain use exists. This is *why* standards-pure
  means resolvability/safety-agnostic, not domain-agnostic.

---

### Suggested order
1. **E** — wire in `IdnaTestV2.txt` (only item that can expose real bugs; proves
   the positioning).
2. **B2 → B** — make `normalization_profile_info()` parametric, then decide
   narrow-flags vs defer.
3. **A** — tighten DESCRIPTION / helper positioning.
4. **C**, **D** — demote URL surface + plan removal; confirm UTS #39 non-goal.
5. **F** — citation/doc sweep (RFC 5892/5893, UAX #15, UTS #46≠IDNA2008).

Primary sources checked: RFC 3492, RFC 5890/5891/5892/5893, UTS #46, WHATWG URL,
RFC 3986, RFC 6874, Unicode 16.0.0 IdnaTestV2.txt.

### Comments

#### 2026-06-16 — 142225707+bart-turczynski@users.noreply.github.com

Folded in expert review (9 notes + scope refinement). Key corrections: dropped the false RFC 5891/IDNA2008 compliance claim for host_normalize (it is a pinned UTS #46 non-transitional profile; UTS #46 != IDNA2008, e.g. coffee.example accepted); split owns/does-not-own scope; renamed canonicalization->normalization (URL canonicalization is rurl); added item B2 (parametric profile identity gates B); corrected the stale test-normalize divergence claim (doc defect on PSLR-pwwtqowh, not a code bug); named the exact 3-flag WHATWG relaxation surface (Bidi/Joiners stay true).

#### 2026-06-16 — 142225707+bart-turczynski@users.noreply.github.com

Second-pass review (Codex), both notes verified against code & folded in: (1) item F RFC 5892 corrected — we implement ContextJ/CheckJoiners (punycoder_normalize.cpp:69-86) but NOT CONTEXTO; CONTEXTO code points marked valid by the UTS-46 mapping table (a*b.cat, Greek keraia, Hebrew geresh/gershayim, Katakana middle dot) are accepted, which is conformant UTS-46, so the issue no longer implies we do full RFC 5892 CONTEXTO validation. (2) B2 sharpened — a zero-arg normalization_profile_info() defaults report cannot describe the profile a flagged call used; it needs matching args or another identity mechanism.




## PUNY-eprrzmxt: Wizard: CRAN submission sequence — pslr -> punycoder -> rurl (gated)

**Status:** done

### Description

## Wizard: CRAN submission sequence — pslr -> punycoder -> rurl (gated on CRAN approval)

### How to run (AI agent)
Guided submission runbook for the coordinated 3-package release. This same issue is filed in **all three repos**, so you can open it from whichever project you are in. Submitting to CRAN is an irreversible outward action: get an explicit "go" from the user for each package before submitting. **Never submit a package until its GATE below is satisfied.** Do not use the AskUserQuestion tool; talk inline.

### Why the order is fixed (do not reorder)
punycoder 1.2.0 REMOVES the `strict` arg from `host_normalize()`. pslr 1.0.1 (currently on CRAN) still calls it. If punycoder 1.2.0 lands first, CRAN's reverse-dependency check runs pslr 1.0.1 against the new punycoder, it errors on the removed arg, and punycoder is rejected. So the consumer that stopped using the removed surface (pslr 1.0.2) must be on CRAN FIRST. rurl floors `pslr >= 1.0.2` + `punycoder >= 1.2.0`, so it is LAST. The "1 submission per 1-2 months" rule is PER PACKAGE, so all three may be submitted in the same week — only the ORDER and the approval GATES matter.

### The sequence

#### Step 1 - pslr 1.0.2  (no upstream gate; submit first)
- Pre-flight: finish the pslr metadata wizard if you want those improvements in the tarball; rebuild; `R CMD check --as-cran` clean (expect 0E/0W/1N, the days-since-update timing note); review `cran-comments.md`.
- Submit (e.g. `devtools::submit_cran()` or the web form).
- **GATE before Step 2:** pslr 1.0.2 is ACCEPTED and LIVE on CRAN. Verify via https://CRAN.R-project.org/package=pslr showing 1.0.2 and `available.packages()`. CRAN sends an auto-ack, then a human decision (often a few days).

#### Step 2 - punycoder 1.2.0  (BLOCKED until Step 1 is live)
- Gate check: confirm pslr 1.0.2 is the CRAN version, so the reverse-dep check no longer sees `strict`.
- Pre-flight: metadata wizard (optional); `--as-cran` Status OK; `cran-comments.md` should note this ships the coordinated removal of the inert `strict` arg and that pslr 1.0.2 (which no longer calls it) is already live. NOTE: this release only DEPRECATES `url_*`/`parse_url`; their removal is a later release (PUNY-rumdaymk).
- Submit.
- **GATE before Step 3:** punycoder 1.2.0 is ACCEPTED and LIVE on CRAN.

#### Step 3 - rurl 1.4.0  (BLOCKED until BOTH Step 1 and Step 2 are live)
- Gate check: pslr >= 1.0.2 AND punycoder >= 1.2.0 both live on CRAN (rurl's dependency floors).
- Pre-flight: metadata wizard (optional, incl. the rurl `_PACKAGE` doc fix); `--as-cran` Status OK; `cran-comments.md` notes the `Remotes:` line is already dropped and the coordinated deps are now live.
- Submit. Done when rurl 1.4.0 is live on CRAN.

### On each acceptance
- Tag the release (`git tag vX.Y.Z` + push the tag).
- Comment on this issue and on that package's metadata wizard.
- Unblock the next step.

### If CRAN bounces a submission
- Address the maintainer comments, bump the patch version if required, re-run `--as-cran`, and resubmit the SAME step. Do not advance the order until the current step is accepted.

### Related
- Metadata wizards: the PUNY/PSLR/RURL "max out ... metadata" issues.
- Release-order rationale is also captured in the rurl umbrella issue RURL-rucvetcl.


### Comments

#### 2026-07-18 — 142225707+bart-turczynski@users.noreply.github.com

Superseded by PSLR-hrpalwzo in ../pslr. The new dependency-aware DAG uses package-specific preparation, compatibility, cran repair+remote, submission, and live-index gates for pslr -> punycoder -> rurl. Preserve this wizard as historical context; do not execute it.




## PUNY-eqttmcuc: Retire the Claude auto-memory store: promote what is durable, delete the rest

**Status:** todo

### Description

Claude's auto-memory is now disabled globally (`autoMemoryEnabled: false` in
~/.claude/settings.json), so this project's store is inert and costs nothing while it sits.
This issue is to recover anything durable from it and then delete it.

### This store, measured

| | |
|---|---|
| Fact files | 12 |
| Size | 22 KB |
| MEMORY.md index | ~542 tokens, injected into every session while memory was on |
| Sessions in this project | 0 |
| Writes (Write/Edit on a memory file) | 0 |
| Explicit reads | 0 |
| Reads in a session that did NOT also write the file | **0** |

Store: `/Users/bartturczynski/.claude/projects/-Users-bartturczynski-Projects-punycoder/memory`

Fleet-wide the ratio was 774 writes to 60 genuine reads, and 93.7% of files were never
genuinely read. Expect most of it to be disposable; look for the few durable method notes.

### Why this is not just a delete

Memories never expire and nothing reconciles them against the repo. In `rurl` several had gone
outright false — a file claiming `cran-comments.md` was untracked when it is tracked, memories
assuming a `Remotes:` field that no longer exists, one asserting `tools/verify.R` was absent from
main when it is present, and three superseded by ADRs that landed after the memory was written.
Skim for durable knowledge, but verify every claim against the tree before promoting it.

### Method (as used for rurl)

Sort every file into four buckets:

1. **Dead** — self-labels as HISTORICAL / CLOSED / RETIRED / FALSIFIED / "kept for the record".
   Delete; git and the tracker own it.
2. **Ephemeral state** — epic/phase status, "T4-T8 remain", "shipped in x.y.z". Delete; NEWS,
   git history and this tracker own it. In rurl these were the *largest* files and the most stale.
3. **Durable and project-specific** — promote into the real docs (AGENTS.md / ARCHITECTURE.md /
   CONTRIBUTING.md / an ADR / a design note). Check first whether the docs already say it; a lot
   of it was re-derived from what was already written down.
4. **Generic, not about this project** — belongs in ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md, if anywhere. Be
   conservative: that file loads in every session in every project.

Prefer consolidating many memories into one coherent doc over transcribing them one-to-one.
In rurl, 14 separate files became a single method note that is worth reading; 32 files were
deleted outright.

### Before deleting

Archive the store first:

```sh
tar -czf ~/Projects/_backups/claude-memory/punycoder-memory-$(date +%F).tar.gz \
    -C "$(dirname '/Users/bartturczynski/.claude/projects/-Users-bartturczynski-Projects-punycoder/memory')" memory
```

### Done when

- [ ] Every file triaged into one of the four buckets
- [ ] Durable items promoted into tracked docs, each claim verified against the tree
- [ ] Store archived to ~/Projects/_backups/claude-memory/
- [ ] Store deleted
- [ ] Any still-open question or live blocker found in it filed as its own issue here

### Precedent

`rurl` (MR !67, merged as d28ea6c): 104 files / 372 KB retired; 5 new design docs + an ADR,
1,076 lines added across 11 files; 32 files deleted as dead or ephemeral.

## PUNY-fqhoaoog: Mint and wire up a citable DOI (Zenodo)

**Status:** done

### Description

### Goal

Mint a citable DOI for this package and wire it back into the repo. This supports the rOpenSci software-review submission and the planned JOSS submission (JOSS requires an archive DOI at acceptance).

### Background

- Two DOIs end up in play and coexist: an **archive DOI** (Zenodo, snapshot of a release) and, later, a **paper DOI** that JOSS mints on acceptance.
- A Zenodo archive DOI does **not** interfere with rOpenSci or JOSS review — JOSS explicitly asks for one near the end of review.
- You get a stable **concept DOI** (always resolves to latest) plus a **version DOI** per release.

### Do as much as possible programmatically

Prefer the scriptable path over clicking through web UIs. Concretely:

1. **`.zenodo.json`** — generate from `DESCRIPTION` (title, authors + ORCID, license, keywords, upstream URL). Controls Zenodo metadata instead of accepting GitHub-scraped defaults. Scriptable.
2. **`CITATION.cff`** — generate with the `cffr` R package from `DESCRIPTION`; add `doi:`/`identifiers:` once the DOI exists. Renders GitHub's "Cite this repository" button. Scriptable.
3. **`inst/CITATION`** — R-native; embed the DOI in `bibentry()` so `citation()` surfaces it. Scriptable.
4. **README badge** — append the Zenodo DOI badge. Scriptable.
5. **Minting itself** — two options:
   - **Zenodo REST API** (fully programmatic): create deposition with a personal token, upload the release tarball, set metadata from `.zenodo.json`, publish → DOI. No UI.
   - **GitHub↔Zenodo integration** (one manual step): flip the per-repo toggle at zenodo.org/account/settings/github once, then publishing a GitHub release auto-archives it. Auto-links to GitHub releases, which is the cleaner provenance for JOSS.

**The only inherently non-programmatic bit** is the one-time Zenodo↔GitHub OAuth authorization (or generating a Zenodo API token). Note in this ticket which route we pick.

### Sequencing caveats

- Don't hardcode a placeholder/fake JOSS paper DOI into `CITATION.cff` — wait for the real one at JOSS acceptance.
- JOSS may ask the archive metadata (title/author list) to match the paper; Zenodo lets you edit record metadata without changing the DOI, so minting early is fine.

### Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Route chosen (REST API vs GitHub integration) and noted
- [ ] `.zenodo.json` generated from `DESCRIPTION`
- [ ] Archive DOI minted (concept + version)
- [ ] `CITATION.cff` updated with the DOI
- [ ] `inst/CITATION` updated with the DOI
- [ ] DOI badge added to README
- [ ] (later) JOSS paper DOI added once accepted

- Version DOI (1.2.0): 10.5281/zenodo.20973630

## PUNY-fsaaigwl: Reduce allocation churn in host_normalize_one (measure after PUNY-thyalpud)

**Status:** done

### Description

Profiling a clean -O2 build under sustained `host_normalize` load puts allocator symbols at the top (`_malloc` 118 samples, `_xzm_free` 40, vs `punycoder::nfc` 41, `host_normalize_one` 55).

Most of that `nfc` cost is what PUNY-thyalpud removes, so **measure again after it lands** before doing any of this. Cheap items first; stop when the profile stops showing them.

- `labels` (src/punycoder_normalize.cpp:343) has no `reserve()` — grows by reallocation, move-constructing a vector and a string per element each time. Trivial, do first.
- `codepoints_to_utf8` reserves `size() * 4` (src/punycoder_utf8.cpp:68). Post-mapping output is ASCII-dominant, so that's a 4x over-allocation on the hottest string in the pipeline. Reserve `size()` and let it grow, or compute the exact width.
- `nfc()` returns by value, allocating two vectors per call. An `nfc_into(in, out&)` overload would let callers reuse one scratch buffer. **Probably not worth the invasiveness once PUNY-thyalpud lands** — only consider if the profile still justifies it.

Gate every step on a measured delta; do not land speculative churn.

### Comments

#### 2026-07-24 — 142225707+bart-turczynski@users.noreply.github.com

Merged as f93dc7d (PR #78). Re-measured after PUNY-thyalpud as the issue required; took the two cheap items, deliberately skipped the third.

Re-measurement (clean -O2, sustained host_normalize, 20k-host corpus ~80% ASCII): the allocator is no longer top of profile. Unicode tables 53.0%, punycoder other 18.6%, libc++/platform 13.9%, allocator 11.7%, R/Rcpp 2.7%.

Landed:
1. labels.reserve() -- count is exactly separator count + 1; growing move-constructs a vector AND a string per LabelWork each realloc.
2. codepoints_to_utf8 reserve size() not size()*4. The 4x was not just slack: it pushes a short ASCII host out of small-string storage onto the heap, buying a malloc the label never needed.

Delta, host_normalize over 400k elements, best-of-15 per cell, clean R CMD INSTALL per config:
  round      base   +labels  +labels+utf8
  1          661      641       626
  2          668      668       640
  3          680      668       648
  4 (rev)    673      659       640
  5 (rev)    669      658       649
  mean      670.2    658.8     640.6

Combined 670.2 -> 640.6 ms, ~4.4%. Full change beats base 5/5 rounds; +utf8 beats +labels 5/5; +labels beats base 4/5 with one tie, no losses. Rounds 4-5 reverse the order to control for thermal drift, which within a round biases against whichever config runs last. Allocator profile share independently falls 11.74% -> 9.83%.
