## PUNY-wfzldcuo: Skip the NFC pipeline when the input is already NFC

**Status:** done | **Parent:** iqduezqtbofgshdtrywtmqrnsgqfflwt

### Description

Surfaced while measuring PUNY-mbzhgbta, and it is a bigger fish than that issue was.

host_normalize_one() calls nfc(mapped) UNCONDITIONALLY (src/punycoder_normalize.cpp:352). There is no quick check, so an all-ASCII host runs the entire decompose -> canonical-order -> compose pipeline to produce a byte-identical copy of its input.

### What that costs, measured

Instrumenting compose_pair() over a 20k-host corpus, per pass:

    frac non-ASCII   compose attempts   of which answered by the b-bound
    0%                        295,792   295,792  (100%)
    20%                       304,830   284,600  (93%)
    50%                       317,170   267,207  (84%)
    100%                      338,892   240,140  (71%)

For the 0% row every one of those 295,792 attempts is pure waste, and so is the decomposition pass that allocated the vector they walk and the canonical_order() scan that called combining_class() on every character.

Self time on an all-non-ASCII corpus after PUNY-mbzhgbta (macOS `sample`, 20,934 samples): nfc() itself 6.3%, combining_class 3.5%, canonical_decomposition 3.0%. Most of the first two exist only to serve nfc().

### Approach

UAX #15 defines NFC_Quick_Check (NFC_QC in DerivedNormalizationProps.txt). A sequence is already in NFC if every character is NFC_QC=Yes and the combining classes are in non-decreasing order within each run. That is one pass with no allocation, and for ASCII it degenerates to a single bound test -- ASCII is entirely NFC_QC=Yes with ccc 0.

Note the table for this is already downloaded: the generator reads DerivedNormalizationProps.txt for Full_Composition_Exclusion, so NFC_QC costs one more parse of a file already in the cache. Emit it the same way as everything else (ADR-011): derived, shape-asserted, and verified against its source ranges over all 1,114,112 code points at generation time.

Watch for: NFC_QC=Maybe is a real third value and must fall through to the full pipeline, not be treated as Yes. Get that wrong and the bug is silent on almost all input.

### Gate

Same as the three issues before it, and do not skip it because a quick check "cannot change the answer" -- that is exactly the claim under test: element-wise host_normalize diff over unique(c(source, to_ascii)) from inst/testdata/IdnaTestV2.txt across all 8 flag combinations (6,403 inputs), extended to is_idn/is_punycode/puny_encode/puny_decode. Better still, diff nfc() against itself with and without the quick check over the NormalizationTest.txt corpus, which is already in data-raw/.ucd-cache/ and is the authoritative test for exactly this.

### Measurement

Both builds installed side by side into separate library trees and alternated -- no rebuild between samples. That protocol (PUNY-mbzhgbta) resolved a 3-5% effect that an A/B/A/B rebuild loop could not separate from noise. Min of 9 batched samples per point, sweep the ASCII fraction.

### Comments

#### 2026-07-25 — 142225707+bart-turczynski@users.noreply.github.com

Implemented and merged as PR #83 (squash 417e1a8).

nfc() now applies the UAX #15 quick check and returns its input unchanged when it passes.

DESIGN. NFC_QC is READ from DerivedNormalizationProps.txt rather than derived -- the generator already parses that file for Full_Composition_Exclusion, so it costs one more pass over a cached file. Same two-stage trie as its neighbours; Yes is the default and covers nearly the whole code space, which is exactly the case block dedup collapses (6.1 KB). Maybe is handled as the real third value the description warned about. The generator also cross-checks the parsed property against the composition pair table derived independently from UnicodeData.txt -- every second element of a pair must not be Yes -- so a mis-parse cannot be silent.

One thing the description did not anticipate, carried over from PUNY-mbzhgbta: the bound in front of the check has to be INLINE. nfc_inert() is emitted into the generated header (U+0300, the lower of the two tables' first listed code point) and applied at the top of the loop, not left to the guards inside combining_class() and nfc_quick_check(), which sit behind a function call. That is what makes the ASCII case one compare per character with no table read and no call.

RESULTS. Two-library alternation, min of 9 batched samples per point, 8 rounds, 20k hosts:

    0% non-ASCII   10.87 -> 8.90 ms   1.22x
   20%             12.45 -> 10.27     1.21x
   50%             14.87 -> 12.23     1.22x
  100%             18.27 -> 15.30     1.19x

All 16 paired comparisons favour the check. Largest single win since ADR-011, and unlike the table work it helps ASCII MOST -- that case was paying the most for nothing. nfc() self time 6.3% -> 2.6%, combining_class 3.5% -> 0.45%; canonical_decomposition and canonical_compose drop below the sampling floor; all table lookups 12.8% -> 6.3%.

WORST CASE, measured rather than argued: the same corpus transformed to NFD, so the check always fails and its pass is pure overhead. Still no regression -- 1.13x / 1.07x / 1.01x at 20/50/100% non-ASCII -- because the check abandons at the first offending character rather than scanning to the end.

Size: __const +6,252 bytes, __text +320; installed .so steps 445,264 -> 462,096 crossing a 16 KB page boundary.

VERIFICATION. Took the description's advice and diffed nfc() against itself with and without the check, which is stronger than the package-surface gate. The harness links both into one binary and tests two invariants -- that the answers match, and that the SKIP DECISION matches whether the full pipeline was a no-op -- over every single code point, all 99,825 sequences in NormalizationTest.txt, 280,887,296 pairs (every code point in planes 0-1 against all 2,143 code points that can affect normalization at all), and 438,976 triples plus 10,000 mark quadruples. Zero disagreements. The same run replays the official UAX #15 corpus through nfc(): all 19,965 rows pass, which is a stronger statement about our NFC than anything previously in the suite. Package gate PASS, byte-identical, 6,403 x 8, extended to the predicates and the codec.

WORTH KNOWING FOR NEXT TIME. I added two testthat cases, one per half of the check, then mutation-tested them. Folding Maybe into Yes failed 6 assertions -- good. Dropping the ORDER test failed NOTHING, because my order test used two NFC_QC=Maybe marks and the property test fires first, so the order test was never reached. The test guarded nothing. Fixed by using U+0316 (ccc 220) before U+0334 (ccc 1), both NFC_QC=Yes, which only the combining-class comparison can catch; that version does fail the mutant. Both mutations are now caught. This is noted in AGENTS.md so the next person does not write the same dead test.

Re-verified on merged main after a clean rebuild: gate PASS, and 9.93 / 11.58 / 13.67 / 16.87 ms across the sweep.

Recorded as ADR-014. AGENTS.md, ARCHITECTURE.md, NEWS.md updated.




## PUNY-wjlfpppq: C: Runtime version selection — pipeline threading and R API surface

**Status:** done | **Parent:** czleeqwznmtmqpuiasoyulxejzawjgfo

### Description

Depends on B (PUNY-kfpxsquq).

Expose the choice to callers and thread it through `host_normalize` /
`normalization_profile_info`.

#### API decision (open)

1. `host_normalize(x, unicode_version = )` — explicit, per-call, matches how the
   three existing UTS-46 knobs (`check_hyphens`, `use_std3`,
   `verify_dns_length`) are already exposed.
2. `getOption("punycoder.unicode_version")` with a `.onLoad` default in
   `R/zzz.R` — matches `punycoder.strict`.
3. Both.

Leaning (1), possibly with (2) as the default source. Note `host_normalize` is
deliberately **not** on the strict/non-strict switch — it always reports invalid
input as `NA` so callers can layer their own policy — so adding a global option
here needs its own justification rather than inheriting that precedent.

#### Validation

An unsupported version must fail loudly and actionably, listing the versions the
build actually shipped. It must not silently fall back to the default: silent
fallback would make a reproducibility key wrong, which is the exact failure
PUNY-nblrvplp was raised to prevent.

#### Profile identity

`normalization_profile_info()` already returns `unicode_version` as its own
column and already accepts the three flags, with
`.normalization_profile_token()` deriving the token (PUNY-nblrvplp). Extend the
same mechanism: the version must be reportable for the exact call that used it,
not just for defaults.

See the epic's open question 3 on whether the token itself changes — leaning no,
since the *profile* (non-transitional, STD3, same flags) is unchanged and the
version column already carries the difference. Confirm with `pslr` (F, PUNY-odzyvuru) first.

### Comments

#### 2026-07-25 — 142225707+bart-turczynski@users.noreply.github.com

C merged: #88 (fc38381). All 11 CI checks green.

Surface: host_normalize(x, ..., unicode_version = NULL), normalization_profile_info(..., unicode_version = NULL), new exported unicode_versions() -> c("16.0.0", "17.0.0"). NULL means the pin, so every existing call is unchanged -- verified, not assumed: 0 differences in 63,128 comparisons (7,891 inputs x 8 flag combos) on the default path vs the merged two-version build.

API decision: option (1), the per-call argument. No getOption() form, deliberately (ADR-016) -- punycoder.strict is error POLICY, the Unicode version is profile IDENTITY (UTS #46: 'Given a version of Unicode...'), and ambient identity would let the same code mint different reproducibility keys in different sessions. NULL means the pin and never 'newest', so a caller who has not thought about versions keeps getting the same answers when a later release adds a table set. An unshipped version errors listing what is available, never falls back.

DIVERGED from the issue's leaning on the profile token: it now appends +unicode-<version> for a non-default set (fixed order, after the flag tags) rather than being left untouched pending an F/pslr check. Rationale: the tag needs no such check because a call at the pin yields the historical token byte-for-byte, so nothing pslr reads today moves; and leaving it untouched would break the token's one promise, that two genuinely different normalizations can never mint identical() tokens. Not a -vN bump -- the profile itself is unchanged. Flagged in the PR body; revisit in F if pslr disagrees.

Also: host_normalize_version_cpp folded into host_normalize_cpp (a test-only parallel entry point can drift from the real one); table-set metadata memoized after measuring it at ~0.75us per call, ~19% of a single-host host_normalize(), now ~0.4us -- invisible on vectorized calls. Contract sections 0.3/3/7/8 updated to separate the pin from per-call selection.

Benchmark unchanged: 0.192 / 0.199 / 0.197 (ascii/unicode/mixed). devtools::test() 520/0/1, lintr clean, R CMD check --as-cran 1 NOTE (dev version string).




## PUNY-womoymke: A: Generator — fix Unicode 17 IDNA URL layout and derive naming from unicode_version

**Status:** done | **Parent:** czleeqwznmtmqpuiasoyulxejzawjgfo

### Description

**Prerequisite for the whole epic.** Two changes to
`data-raw/generate_unicode_tables.R`.

#### 1. The IDNA data files moved in Unicode 17 (hard blocker)

`idna_base` (line 25) 404s at 17.0.0. Unicode relocated the IDNA directory:

```
https://www.unicode.org/Public/idna/17.0.0/IdnaMappingTable.txt   -> 404
https://www.unicode.org/Public/17.0.0/idna/IdnaMappingTable.txt   -> 200
```

The path segments swap: `Public/idna/<ver>` becomes `Public/<ver>/idna`. The
`ucd_base` layout (`Public/<ver>/ucd`) is unchanged. The 17.0.0 `idna/` dir holds
`Idna2008.txt`, `IdnaMappingTable.txt`, `IdnaTestV2.txt`, `ReadMe.txt`.

Note `Public/idna/latest/` *is* updated to 17.0 and is byte-identical to
`Public/17.0.0/idna/` — but pinning to `latest` would defeat the entire vendoring
design. Take the versioned path. Ideally handle both layouts so the generator can
still produce a <=16.0.0 table set (needed by B, PUNY-kfpxsquq).

#### 2. Derive the emitted naming from `unicode_version`

Currently hardcoded in the generator and therefore in its output:

- output filenames `src/unicode_tables_16_0_0.{h,cpp}` (lines 835, 1087)
- header guard `PUNYCODER_UNICODE_TABLES_16_0_0_H` (line 746)
- C++ namespace `u16` (lines 757, 827, 843, 1083)

All three must come from `unicode_version`, in the same derived-not-hand-written
spirit as ADR-011/ADR-012 that already governs every constant, array element
type, and trie block size in this file. This is what makes a version bump one
line instead of a 19-file sweep, and it is what lets B emit two versions side by
side without a collision.

#### Verification

Re-running at 16.0.0 must still reproduce the committed
`src/unicode_tables_16_0_0.cpp` byte-for-byte (confirmed to hold today — keep it
as the regression gate).

### Comments

#### 2026-07-25 — 142225707+bart-turczynski@users.noreply.github.com

Done in #84 (69a5716).

Both parts landed:
1. IDNA layout — `idna_bases` now tries `Public/<ver>/idna` then `Public/idna/<ver>`, newest-first, so 17.0.0 works and <=16.0.0 still does. Not `latest/`.
2. Naming derived — output filenames, header guard, and C++ namespace all come from `unicode_version` (`table_stem`/`table_ns`/`guard`).

Also fixed a latent bug the epic would have tripped: the UCD cache was flat (`data-raw/.ucd-cache/`) and keyed on filename only, so a 17.0.0 run would have silently reused 16.0.0's UnicodeData.txt. Now scoped per version.

Verification: re-running at 16.0.0 reproduces src/unicode_tables_16_0_0.{h,cpp} byte-for-byte (git diff empty, re-checked after the lint fixup). 17.0.0 fetches the new layout with no fallback and generates zero-assertion, emitting u17 / PUNYCODER_UNICODE_TABLES_17_0_0_H. Those artifacts were not committed — they belong to B.

Note for B (PUNY-kfpxsquq): the 17.0.0 UTS-46 trie picks block 128 (stage1 7172 x uint8_t, stage2 32640 x uint16_t, 70.8 KB) where 16.0.0 picks block 64 (77.9 KB) — the shapes differ per version, so B cannot assume a shared block size across the two units.




## PUNY-wqmwuvtt: Bound print.punycoder_validation output; surface error_codes; add summary() method

**Status:** done

### Description

`print.punycoder_validation` (R/results.R:31) loops `cat` over every element, so printing `validate_domain(x)` for a 20k vector dumps 20k blocks. It also never shows `error_codes` — the machine-readable surface added deliberately in PUNY-qytksjpd — so the documented feature is undiscoverable from the console.

### Scope
- Truncate output with an '... and N more' footer (follow the tibble/testthat convention for the cutoff).
- Show `error_codes` alongside `errors`.
- Promote the existing internal `get_validation_summary()` (R/results.R:10) to a registered `summary.punycoder_validation` method. Only `print` is in NAMESPACE today.

### Design decision needed
What `summary()` returns: per-domain messages (what `get_validation_summary()` does now — one string per element) or an aggregate (n valid / n invalid, counts by error code). Aggregate is the more conventional reading of `summary()` for a vectorized result, and the per-domain view is already what `print()` gives. Decide before implementing.

### Comments

#### 2026-07-24 — 142225707+bart-turczynski@users.noreply.github.com

Design decision: summary() returns an AGGREGATE, not per-domain messages.

Rationale:
1. print() already gives the per-domain view. Two methods differing only in verbosity is not worth a public API slot.
2. A summary() that returns one element per input is not a summary. R convention (summary.factor, summary.lm) is condensation.
3. It makes error_codes pay off. That field was added in PUNY-qytksjpd as the machine-readable surface; aggregating by code answers the real question when validating 10k domains -- what is wrong, and how much of it.
4. Nothing is lost: the per-domain detail is already reachable via result$errors / result$error_codes, and the internal get_validation_summary() stays as-is for print().

Shape: return a data.frame of error_code x n sorted descending, carrying n / n_valid / n_invalid as attributes, with its own print method so it stays programmable rather than print-only. Sketch:

  Punycoder validation summary (strict = TRUE)
  10,000 domains: 3 valid, 9,997 invalid

    error_code                    n
    domain_label_too_long     9,000
    ascii_domain_characters     997

Decided by Claude on the maintainer's delegation; cheap to revisit before release since nothing depends on it yet.

#### 2026-07-24 — 142225707+bart-turczynski@users.noreply.github.com

Landed as 3c77b77 (PR #70). print() bounded at 10 blocks + '... and N more' footer + count header + [error_code] bullets; summary.punycoder_validation returns the aggregate data.frame (error_code x n, desc) with n/n_valid/n_invalid/strict attributes and its own print method.

Two things found during implementation worth recording:
1. The design comment's rationale #4 was WRONG: get_validation_summary() is NOT used by print() (print inlines its own cat loop) and never was. Its only consumers are 3 test call sites in test-validators.R. Kept it and corrected the stale roxygen line; it is effectively dead in production and is a fair candidate for removal in a later cleanup.
2. _pkgdown.yml has an EXPLICIT reference index whose Internals section matched only starts_with('print.'). pkgdown hard-errors on unlisted topics, so the new summary. method would have failed the pkgdown workflow. Broadened to starts_with('summary.').

## PUNY-ypjwnagl: Fallback puny_decode accepts non-LDH chars in A-label input (libidn2 rejects)

**Status:** done

### Description

## Fallback `puny_decode` accepts non-LDH characters in A-label input (libidn2 rejects)

Found while running a backend-parity check for the punycoder R Journal paper
(`_scratch/paper/idna-bench/backend_parity.R`, §3.8 of `_scratch/paper/PAPER-PLAN.md`).
Directly downstream of the concern already raised in **PUNY-urifwrpn** (`strict=FALSE`
drops structural/LDH validation).

### What happens

With the default `automatic = "libidn2+fallback"` backend (libidn2 tried first, in-tree
fallback on **exception**), the two backends disagree on **58** malformed decode inputs
harvested from spec-invalid IdnaTestV2 rows. Every disagreement is the same shape:
**the in-tree fallback accepts and decodes; libidn2 rejects** with
`"string contains invalid punycode data"`. Zero reverse cases; zero both-accept-differ.
57/58 inputs contain a non-LDH character (`,` `%` `?` `(` `)`).

Because `automatic` catches libidn2's rejection and falls through, the permissive result
wins at the **public** API:

```r
puny_decode("xn--(o)-ge4ax01c3t74t")  # -> "⒈…ⴓ(o)"   ( ) in an A-label
puny_decode("xn--6,-r4e6182wo1ra")    # -> "…6,𐼗︒"     comma
puny_decode("xn---%-u4o")             # -> "-ᠹ%"       percent sign
```

### Why it may be wrong

The DESCRIPTION advertises that `puny_encode()` / `puny_decode()` "perform the raw
transform plus letter-digit-hyphen checks". These inputs violate LDH on the *input*
label, yet pass. Either the promise is decode-input-inclusive (then this is a bug), or it
is encode/output-only (then the DESCRIPTION wording should be tightened so the two
backends' contracts match).

### Scope / decision

- Should the fallback decode path LDH-validate its input label the way libidn2 does, so
  the two backends agree on rejection as well as on output?
- Interacts with PUNY-urifwrpn's `strict` redesign: LDH validation is exactly the

## PUNY-zgaqusnu: Consolidate generated Unicode table lookups + ASCII fast path

**Status:** done

### Description

Split out of PUNY-ktbbdbho (last bullet) and PARKED at the 2026-07-24 orchestration gate — deliberately not run in that batch.

unicode_tables_16_0_0.cpp emits SEVEN near-identical binary searches (combining_class, canonical_decomposition, canonical_compose, idna_lookup, is_combining_mark, bidi_class, joining_type). Collapsing the GENERATOR to one range_lookup template would make an ASCII fast path (cp < 0x80 skips ~13 probes/char for the dominant input) a one-line change in one place.

Why parked, not dropped: this is the highest remaining perf upside in the backlog, but it rewrites generated tables and cannot be reviewed from a small diff. It needs its own session with the conformance-diff harness rebuilt.

Gate before landing: diff host_normalize output element-wise over unique(c(corpus$source, corpus$to_ascii)) from inst/testdata/IdnaTestV2.txt across all 8 combinations of check_hyphens/use_std3/verify_dns_length (6,407 inputs x 8 flag sets).

Constraints confirmed by blast-radius probe: all seven lookups are internal to src/ (no LinkingTo, no sourceCpp, siblings cannot reach them), so signatures are safe to change. Derive any ASCII table IN the generator so it cannot drift from the UCD source. inst/testdata/IdnaTestV2.txt is byte-sensitive and excluded from pre-commit fixers.

### Comments

#### 2026-07-24 — 142225707+bart-turczynski@users.noreply.github.com

Fresh measurement for this issue's gate, from the profiling run that closed PUNY-fsaaigwl and PUNY-cwtxlabr (2026-07-25, clean -O2 build, sustained host_normalize over a 20k-host corpus ~80% ASCII, macOS arm64, libidn2 backend).

This is now confirmed as the largest remaining target in the package, by a wide margin.

Unicode table lookups = 53.0% of process time before PUNY-fsaaigwl, 56.0% after (share of a smaller total):

  u16::canonical_compose         13.6%
  u16::idna_lookup               11.5%
  u16::combining_class           11.0%
  u16::bidi_class                 8.3%
  u16::canonical_decomposition    7.6%
  u16::is_combining_mark          1.0%

For scale, everything else: punycoder other 18.6%, libc++/platform 13.9%, allocator 11.7% (now 9.8%), R/Rcpp boundary 2.7%.

Table sizes confirming the probe-depth estimate in the description: IDNA_N 9185, DECOMP_N 2081, BIDI_N 1587, COMP_N 961, JOINING_N 519, CCC_N 393, MARK_N 321. IDNA_N=9185 is ~14 data-dependent, branch-mispredicting iterations per code point.

Two refinements to the plan:
- canonical_compose is the single largest line item but is keyed on a PAIR of code points, so it does not fit the same range_lookup shape as the other six. It needs its own treatment.
- combining_class and is_combining_mark are trivially 0/false for all ASCII, and bidi_class is a small fixed set over ASCII, so those three may need only an early return rather than a table.

Also worth carrying in: the allocator work already took the cheap wins next door (PUNY-fsaaigwl, ~4.4%), and a measurement caution learned in PUNY-cwtxlabr -- "fewer passes" is not automatically faster. A hand-rolled single pass there measured 0.81x because each std::string::find lowers to a vectorized memchr that a scalar loop cannot beat. Do not assume a scalar fast path wins; measure it.

Note PUNY-nhqnuubd was filed for this before I found this issue -- closing that as the duplicate; this one is the canonical record.

#### 2026-07-25 — 142225707+bart-turczynski@users.noreply.github.com

Starting. Plan: (1) build the element-wise conformance-diff harness and capture a baseline from HEAD before touching anything, (2) rewrite the generator's emit section to one shared range_lookup + a point_lookup, (3) derive the fast paths in the generator from the UCD data, (4) clean rebuild, run the 6407x8 gate, benchmark.

#### 2026-07-25 — 142225707+bart-turczynski@users.noreply.github.com

Implemented and pushed as PR #80.

Shape of the fix, per accessor, all DERIVED in the generator:
- ccc / marks / decomposition / joining_type: list nothing below U+0080, so a bounds test against their own first/last listed code point answers ASCII with zero memory access. First entries are U+0300, U+0300, U+00C0, U+00AD.
- idna_lookup / bidi_class: cover ASCII, so no bounds test can skip them -> 128-entry direct index. idna emits the range INDEX (uint16, IDNA_N=9185 fits) rather than the status, so the fast and slow paths return the identical IdnaRange and the mapping-data pointer is computed in one place.
- canonical_compose: your note was right that it does not fit range_lookup. The treatment it needed turned out to be cheap: bound the SECOND element only. min(b)=0x300, max(b)=0x16D67 over all 961 pairs, and only 72 distinct b values. A bound on a would NOT work -- min(a)=0x3C. This matters more than it looks: in nfc() the compose_pair() call fires for every character whose predecessor is a starter, which for pure ASCII is every character, which is why it profiled as the single largest line item at 13.6%.

Searches went 7 -> 2 templates (range_lookup + key_lookup for the point-keyed decomp index) + compose's own pair search.

Results (clean -O2, 20k hosts, best-of-5, both build orders):
  0% non-ASCII   14.98/14.77 -> 8.30/8.45 ms   1.75x
  20%            22.77/23.05 -> 16.40/16.92    1.36x
  50%            34.72/35.25 -> 28.43/29.23    1.21x
  100%           54.15/54.80 -> 47.40/49.05    1.12x
Nothing regressed. Heeded your PUNY-cwtxlabr caution and measured rather than assumed -- but this is not the memchr case: replacing a mispredicting binary search with a direct index is a different mechanism, and the template indirection cost nothing (clang inlines it fully). The all-non-ASCII gain is real too, because those hosts still carry ASCII TLDs/dots/digits and the <0x300 bounds skip most of the BMP, not just ASCII.

Gate: 6,403 unique inputs x all 8 flag combinations, byte-identical. Extended it to is_idn/is_punycode/puny_encode/puny_decode over the same corpus as well. All 6,007 pre-existing table data rows unchanged -- the generated diff is purely mechanism -- and unicode_tables_16_0_0.h is untouched, so the native API is unchanged.

Two incidental findings:
1. Control run first: regenerating from the UNMODIFIED generator did not reproduce the committed files. Two cosmetic drifts -- the .h banner and one hand-reflowed accessor body had been hand-edited despite the DO NOT EDIT BY HAND banner. Both fixed. Worth doing this control on any future table change; it is what makes the later diff trustworthy.
2. The generator now asserts the shape it assumed (stops if a future Unicode version extends a bounds-tested table into ASCII, or gives a composition pair an ASCII second element) rather than silently emitting a guard that would skip real data.

Recorded as ADR-011; AGENTS.md and ARCHITECTURE.md updated with the derivation invariant and the gate command.

#### 2026-07-25 — 142225707+bart-turczynski@users.noreply.github.com

Merged as #80 (squash 77b8d57). Re-verified on merged main after a clean rebuild: gate PASS (byte-identical, 6403 x 8), 16.55 ms/pass vs the 23.35-23.85 baseline.

Two corrections to things I got wrong mid-flight, for the record:
1. Your comment predicted combining_class/is_combining_mark/bidi_class 'may need only an early return rather than a table'. True for the first two, NOT for bidi_class -- ASCII Bidi classes are heterogeneous (L/EN/ES/CS/ON/BN/B/S/WS), so it needed the same 128-entry direct index as the UTS-46 table. Only the tables that list nothing below U+0080 (ccc, marks, decomposition, joining) can use a bounds test.
2. I initially commented the generator's assertions as preventing 'a guard that skips real data'. That is wrong: every bound is derived from the table it guards, so it stays correct whatever the data does. What a Unicode bump could break is the SHAPE choice -- a bounds-tested table growing into ASCII would quietly stop hitting its fast path, a silent perf regression with no wrong answer to expose it. Corrected in the generator, ADR-011 and AGENTS.md before merge, and the decomposition index was added to the asserted set (bounds-tested but originally omitted).

Note the gate corpus is 6,403 unique inputs, not the 6,407 in the description -- that is what tests/testthat/helper-idna.R's parser yields after dropping unpaired-surrogate rows. Used the repo's own parser rather than re-deriving one.

Remaining headroom, if anyone wants it later: non-ASCII still binary-searches. A two-stage trie over idna_lookup would make it O(1) for all code points, but it blows up table size and is a much larger generator rewrite than this was. The 100%-non-ASCII case only improved 1.12x, so that is where the remaining upside sits.

## PUNY-zumspyzy: Unwrap the \donttest{} on the five core help pages so CRAN actually runs the primary examples

**Status:** done

### Description

Found by the CRAN pre-submission gate, 2026-07-26. Not a release blocker and
not coupled to the 1.3.0 tag gate (PUNY-tjusxhgn) -- this is independent of
release timing and of the rurl/pslr coordination.

### What

All five core help pages wrap their ENTIRE `\examples{}` block in
`\donttest{}`:

  - man/puny_encode.Rd
  - man/puny_decode.Rd
  - man/is_idn.Rd
  - man/is_punycode.Rd
  - man/validate_domain.Rd

`R CMD check` skips `\donttest{}` by default, so CRAN's routine checks never
execute the examples for the package's primary surface. All 8 exports have
examples, but only 3 of the 8 help pages actually run under a default check.

The fix is in the roxygen blocks in R/punycoder.R and R/validators.R, not in
man/ -- the .Rd files are generated. Regenerate with
`Rscript -e 'roxygen2::roxygenise()'` and commit both.

### Why these don't need \donttest

Inspected during the gate run: every one of these examples is fast, offline,
deterministic, and free of long-running calls. They are literal
encode/decode/predicate calls on string constants. There is no network, no
filesystem, no timing dependence, and nothing that varies by platform or
backend -- the libidn2-vs-fallback parity tests already assert the two agree
on exactly this kind of input.

`R CMD check --run-donttest` passed clean in the 2026-07-26 gate run, which is
direct evidence that unwrapping is safe rather than an assumption.

The `\donttest{}` was most likely defensive boilerplate from the initial
scaffold rather than a considered decision about these specific calls; if
there was a reason, it is not recorded anywhere in the repo.

### Value

Unwrapping converts five help pages from documentation CRAN never executes
into documentation CRAN verifies on every platform it checks -- including the
Windows fallback-backend path, which is the configuration least covered by
local development (configure only defines -DPUNYCODER_USE_LIBIDN2 on
Linux/macOS, so Windows builds always exercise the in-tree fallback). That
makes this a small but genuine cross-platform signal, not just cosmetics.

### Acceptance

  - The five roxygen blocks no longer wrap their examples in \donttest{}.
  - `roxygen2::roxygenise()` run, and R/ and man/ committed together.
  - `R CMD check` WITHOUT --run-donttest executes all five, 0 errors.
  - Example runtime stays well inside CRAN's per-example budget.

### Not in scope

The release version string, NEWS heading, and cran-comments rewrite -- those
are deferred to the ~2026-08-19 window per PUNY-tjusxhgn.
